name: Yaniv Oren
title: PhD candidate in deep reinforcement learning, TUDelft
bio:
I'm a Deep Reinforcement Learning (RL, DRL) scientist and visiting researcher in CWI, the Dutch research institute for Mathematics and Computer Science. I'm also in the process of finalizing my PhD at TU Delft.
 
My research abstracts RL as seperate, interacting processes of policy improvement. Driven by this view, my work aims to optimize the process of policy improvement itself:
In Epistemic Monte Carlo Tree Search (EMCTS, ICLR 2025) we've developed the required machinery to extend search, one of the most powerful policy improvement operators in RL, to optimizing data gathering (e.g. exploration) policies.

In Value Improved Actor Critic Algorithms (VIAC, NeurIPS 2025) we've shown that the evaluation policy can and should be viewed as a distinct policy in the RL process. By separately improving the evaluation policy (value improvement), the performance of seminal RL algorithms (SAC and TD3) is significantly increased, at no increased cost.

In Twice Sequential Monte Carlo for Tree Search (TSMCTS, in review in ICML 2026) we've developed a novel search-based policy improvement operator. TSMCTS bridges Monte Carlo Tree Search and Sequential Monte Carlo for search in RL, harnessing mechanisms from one to address shortcomings in the other, resulting in a novel method that outperforms both at the computational cost of the cheaper of the two.

In collaboration with peers, we have recently published additional work, spanning uncertainty quantification, bridging the gap between target based and target free RL and enhancing policy improvement with trust region optimization:
1. Universal Value-Function Uncertainties. Moritz A. Zanger, Max Weltevrede, Yaniv Oren, Pascal R. Van der Vaart, Caroline Horsch, Wendelin Böhmer, Matthijs T. J. Spaan. ICLR 2026.
2. Bridging the performance-gap between target-free and target-based reinforcement learning.. Théo Vincent, Yogesh Tripathi, Tim Faust, Yaniv Oren, Jan Peters, Carlo D'Eramo. ICLR 2026.
3. Trust-Region Twisted Policy Improvement. Joery A. de Vries, Jinke He, Yaniv Oren, Matthijs T. J. Spaan. ICML 2025.

Prior to embarking on this AI/ML/RL journey, I had the opportunity to be a team lead for several years in a dynamic environment, managing complex projects with innovative requirements, demanding timelines, limited budget & resources, involving research and data analysis.

I am interested in opportunities to lead and contribute to research with real impact, combining deep reinforcement learning expertise with the leadership and management skills I developed prior to my research career.

name: Nisheet Patel
title: Machine Learning Research Scientist and Engineer
bio:
I am a machine learning researcher and engineer with a strong background in theoretical neuroscience. My research interests span from reinforcement learning and control to decision-making and understanding human and animal behavior. I did my PhD with Alex Pouget at the University of Geneva where I worked on normative theories of decision-making, memory-limited agents, and world models as well as musculoskeletal control with Deep RL and exploring theoretical links of Deep RL to normative resource-limited RL models. 

Currently, I am developing tools for researchers to enhance the tedious academic experience, starting with Axy's web app for scientific conferences with powerful search, recommendations, and agenda management. On the side, I'm very keen on science communication and education, and regularly teach RL courses at all levels from high-school kids to PhD/post-doc-level students.

title:
PhD Student @ UC Riverside

• Natural Language Processing, Large Reasoning Model, Multi-modal Large Language Model, Trustworthy AI

• Looking for Summer 2026 Internship
bio: Hi! I am a second-year Ph.D. student at University of California, Riverside with a 4.00 CGPA, specializing in Trustworthy AI and Large Reasoning Models. My research directly addresses safety and transparency in generative AI, evidenced by my recent publication at EMNLP 2024 on text-to-image adversarial attacks and my current work on modeling hierarchical thinking in reasoning models. I am also actively investigating multimodal alignment blind spots (accepted at ICLR 2026), aiming to make Vision-Language Models more robust and reliable. I have a strong track record in low-resource multi-lingual NLP and Software Engineering, with a published paper in ASE 2023 on contrastive learning for API analysis. In addition to my research, I have nearly five years of academic leadership experience as a Lecturer and research supervisor, where I mentored students on Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Gender Bias Mitigation. I was a former ACM ICPC regional contestant. My technical proficiency spans Python, C++, and PyTorch, with expertise in LLM optimization techniques like Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), Adversarial Training and model interpretability methods like Contrastive Activation Steering, LIME.

name: Arnav Goel

bio: Hello! My name is Arnav Goel and I am a graduate student in the Machine Learning Department at Carnegie Mellon University (CMU). My research interests lie in building explainable, trustworthy, and inclusive machine learning systems and LLMs, with recent focus on improving pre-/post-training paradigms, exploring non-transformer architectures, and enabling efficient reasoning in LLMs. I have published first-author papers at top venues including ACM Multimedia 2025, ICLR 2025, AAAI 2025, AAAI 2024, ICLR 2024, and INTERSPEECH 2024. Previously, I worked as a Research Intern at Microsoft Research, where I developed reasoning frameworks for LLM-driven recommendations in Bing Search, created a benchmark for large-scale user modeling, and designed efficient distillation pipelines for SLM-based recommenders. I have also been selected amongst 15 students across India for the prestigious IUSSTF-Viterbi Research Program 2024 and the MITACS Globalink Research Scholarship, which allowed me to pursue fully funded research internships at the University of Southern California and Mila–Quebec AI Institute respectively. I am currently looking for Summer 2026 internships in Machine Learning Engineering/Research, NLP, Applied Science, and Quant Research. Please feel free to reach out if you think I may be a good fit. Get in touch with me: arnavgoe@cs.cmu.edu

To build scalable, trustworthy AI solutions — especially for resource-constrained environments — that bridge the gap between cutting-edge research and real-world applications. 🧠 Key Strengths: • LLMOps & MLOps expertise • Proficient in PyTorch, Hugging Face, BERT, Transformers • Strong in NLP, few-shot learning, and evaluation frameworks • End-to-end experience from research to deployment • Cross-functional collaboration, teaching & mentoring (500+ students taught) 🌎 Previously, I’ve worked with Google-Talentsprint, Major League Hacking, and open-source communities, contributing to both academic and applied AI problems. ✅ Currently open to: • ML/NLP/LLM Engineer roles • AI Research positions (industry) • Internships or part-time roles in MLOps/LLMOps Let’s connect if you're looking for someone who brings deep technical expertise, a researcher's curiosity, and a builder's mindset.

name: Raj Tomar
title: Researcher | Software Developer | Intern @MBZUAI | Python, Data Analysis, Prompt Engineering, Machine learning, OpenAI, ChatGPT
bio:
Hey!
Glad that you stumbled over my profile:)

I'm a researcher and engineer working at the intersection of Large Language Models, reasoning safety, and multilingual NLP. My work focuses on improving generalization, safety alignment, and retrieval-centric (RAG) reasoning in large-scale transformer models through mid-training, instruction fine-tuning, and systematic evaluation across benchmarks. I have led the development of a 120B-parameter in-house LLM and contributed to peer-reviewed publications at EMNLP, COLING, and IJCNLP. My interests also include model interpretability, domain adaptation, and building reliable AI systems for real-world applications.

Story till now!!

Being a decent student in school, I'm more into academics. I was amongst the top 1% scorer (all over India) in the intermediate exams 2021. But it's not like I didn't do anything else at school. I participated at National level Quiz competition at IIT Delhi, zonal level silver medalist at chess, served as Captain of Red group and much more...….

Taking certain hard decisions, I joined CIC. CIC was peaceful with a great learning environment. Whatever I do today CIC has a great role to play in it. At CIC, I learned how to code, how to manage deadlines, how to work in team, how to manage team, how to mentor people, and most importantly the confidence to say yes to any work.

I would love to talk :) feel free to reach out.

name: Shang Sim
title: ML @ Oumi AI
bio: 🚀 Hi, I am Shang Hong! Currently, I am building open source with Oumi! Previously, I was a Master's student at the DeCLaRE Lab, advised by Prof. Soujanya Poria. My research focused on addressing core limitations of Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly hallucinations, as they increasingly serve as information consolidators 🧠. I developed a novel metric to evaluate LLM groundedness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems and proposed a preference dataset to align models for improved grounding 🎯. My prior work spans interdisciplinary applications, including leveraging Unity3D to bridge vision and language tasks 👀 and utilizing bioinformatics to identify therapeutically significant gene sets 🧬. With experience in state-of-the-art NLP and cancer biology, I hope to contribute experimental and analytical expertise to the projects that I am part of. I am passionate about advancing cutting-edge research and translating complex findings into practical, impactful solutions that drive both technical and business innovation 💡.

bio: Research Scientist with 5+ years of experience in researching and developing AI systems, including high-stakes applications (e.g., healthcare, education). My expertise spans across several fields of AI: - LLM Pretraining & Post-training: Pretrained large encoders with masked language modeling; applied RL (e.g., GRPO) and SFT to improve reasoning, alignment, and personalization. - LLM Uncertainty & Safety: Developed algorithms to quantify hallucination risk and detect incomplete information in high-stakes domains. - LLM Benchmark & Evaluation: Designed and collected new benchmark datasets for LLM tutors. - LLM Deployment: Deployed an LLM tutoring system used by 600+ students over a school year. My research has been published in leading scientific venues such as ICML, PNAS, and ITCS. It has had significant impact, including being cited in the 2025 Economic Report of the President, submitted by the U.S. President to the Congress. My Hugging Face models have been downloaded more than 1,100 times.

name: Ganesh Venkatesh
title: Making Machines Smarter
bio: Leading Post-training research for Waymo's Planning and World Behavior models to advance the next generation of autonomous driving intelligence. Prior to this, I helped start and lead AppliedML @ Cerebras -- team of ML scientists working on advancements in training and deploying multimodal models that can reason over infinite context. Our accomplishments have been covered by multiple news outlets such as Forbes, Business Wire, TechCrunch among others. Highlights include: - State-of-the-art Genomics foundation model in collaboration with Mayo, advancing research in drug response prediction. - The CePO line of work, which leverages inference-time compute for enhanced reasoning and infinite context support. - Regionally customized multilingual models such as Jais (Arabic) and Nanda (Hindi) that capture nuances of the local dialect. Prior to this, I led a team of AI Research Scientist at Facebook and were lucky to have driven multiple seminal efforts -- on-device speech-to-text models, multi-modal contextual AI pipeline, open source release of PyTorchVideo mobile, 3D Holograms among others. I also started the On-device Intelligence Workshop at MLSys and helped organize first two editions of it. In my past life, experienced in both training low-precision/sparse DL networks as well as developing hardware architecture features (led from conception to PoR Sparse Tensor support in Nvidia Ampere GPU, INT4 support in Nvidia Turing) to accelerate them. Strong academic foundation with a Ph.D. in Computer Science from University of California, San Diego.

title: Senior Robotics/AI Engineer
bio: I currently work at Figure AI in the Helix team developing loco-manipulation control using AI (deep RL and imitation learning) that enables humanoid robots to interact with their surroundings fully autonomously. I also contribute to distillation, field calibration using perception and behaviors design. Before, I was a postdoctoral research fellow at the Hybrid Systems Lab, University of California Berkeley, where I worked with Prof. Claire J. Tomlin on safe quadrupedal robot navigation in cluttered environments. I earned my PhD in Computer Science, supervised by Prof. Sebastian Trimpe, and co-advised by Prof. Philipp Hennig and Prof. Sten Schaal at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Tübingen, Germany.

name: Nikhil Sridhar
title: Research Engineer @ Skild AI | prev Masters CSE @ University of Michigan
bio: I am a member of technical staff at Skild AI where I will focus on building robotics foundation models for cross-embodiment learning. Previously, I did my Masters at the University of Michigan studying computer science and theoretical math. name: Valerio Ciaurro
title: Postdoc at MD Anderson Cancer Center
bio:
Dynamic scientist with a Ph.D. and 8 years of extensive experience in hematology, oncology, and leukemia research, with a strong focus on hematopoietic stem cells and acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Proven track record in translational research, including preclinical drug evaluation and mechanism-of-action studies. Expertise in CRISPR screening, flow cytometry, and in vivo models. Excellent communicator with strong skills in presenting complex scientific data to both scientific and non-scientific audiences. Adept at fostering collaborations across teams, ensuring data accuracy, and providing scientific insights to guide therapeutic development. Now looking to leverage my scientific background and communication skills in a role where I can support the development and application of new therapeutic strategies.

-Key Skills:
Expertise in oncology, hematology, and cell therapy, with in-depth knowledge of CAR-T technologies and
leukemia biology.
• Strong foundation in clinical trial design, data interpretation, and preclinical-to-clinical translation, including
providing support for investigator-initiated trials by assisting in trial design and execution.
• Experienced in CRISPR screening, flow cytometry, CyTOF, and lentiviral infection.
• Involved in strategic clinical development discussions, contributing to clinical trial strategy and development.
• Proficient in developing cross-functional collaborations, KOL engagement, and scientific data dissemination.
• Skilled in adapting to fast-paced biotech environments and driving impactful scientific strategies.
• Effective communicator, capable of engaging diverse stakeholders including healthcare professionals, academic
leaders, and patient groups.

name: Laura Garcia-gerique
title: Research specialist in immuno-oncology | Cell&molecular biology | Philadelphia
bio:
Driven by curiosity and enthusiasm, I have pursued a research-focused career guided by a passion for advancing patient-centric science that delivers tangible societal benefits.

Experienced scientist with a strong foundation in tumor microenvironment research and cellular immunotherapy. My work includes publishing over 10 indexed scientific articles in immuno-oncology and developing GMP-compliant manufacturing processes for next-generation T cell activation platforms designed for clinical applications.

Skilled leader and problem solver who thrives in multidisciplinary settings. I excel in team leadership, effective communication of complex scientific concepts, and aligning cross-functional efforts toward shared goals, supported by strong organizational skills and a collaborative mindset.

I'm always up for discussing science, and I'm interested in learning about any new projects or opportunities to make a difference!

name: Ankur Saikia
title: Postdoctoral Scientist- Protein Biochemistry • Drug Discovery • Bioassays • Immunotherapy • Strain Engineer • Process Development• Project Management •
location: Copenhagen, Capital Region of Denmark, Denmark
bio: As a Postdoctoral Researcher at DTU - Technical University of Denmark, I optimize the production and process development of MHC proteins for scale-up manufacturing, in alignment with the regulatory requirements of good manufacturing practices (cGMP), for ongoing cancer-immunotherapy clinical trials with PokeAcell Aps (Copenhagen). I also perform quality control assessments and characterization of the purified MHC monomers, using various analytical techniques such as ELISA, fluorescence polarization, nanoDSF, and microscale thermophoresis. I have a strong background in protein production and characterization, bioassay development, and lab automation for HTS platforms, with 11 years of industrial and 7 years of academic experience. I have successfully delivered 11 drug discovery projects, developed in collaboration with prominent pharmaceutical companies, encompassing crucial areas such as hit identification, lead optimization, and drug safety profiling. I am passionate about applying my skills and knowledge to advance the field drug discovery.

bio: I’m a Research Scientist on the SecureBio AI team, where I focus on assessing the scientific capabilities of AI systems and building safeguards to mitigate risks arising from misuse. AI reminds me of fire: it transformed human evolution and helped build civilisation, but it can also destroy; it’s all about control. While it is crucial to protect against the risks of AIxBio misuse, preserving AI’s beneficial uses in scientific research is equally important. I’m a virologist by training, with a long-standing interest in pandemic preparedness. I pivoted into AI biosecurity upon the realisation that biological expertise and wet-lab experience can help inform technical work and mitigation strategies that are grounded and robust. I also believe that there is a narrow window to put effective mitigations in place against AI-enabled biorisks, and that window is now!

name: Nikita Mundhara
title: Post-doctoral fellow @ Johns Hopkins School of Medicine | Tumor Immunotherapy | Graphologist | Remote Academic Mentor @ IMERXN
bio: Passionate about investigating cell-based therapy, CAR-T therapy, and immunotherapy for cancer. At Johns Hopkins Medicine, my team and I delve into the intricacies of tumor immunology, leveraging over two years of postdoctoral research to unravel the potential of checkpoint blockade therapy. My expertise in Tumor immunology is complemented by a strong foundation in mammalian cell culture, CRISPR-Cas9 technology, 40-color spectral flow cytometry, 18-color cytokine Luminex assays, and skills honed through rigorous academic and practical application. I am passionate about working as a team in cancer immunotherapy, contributing and gaining expertise in growing organizations. I love practicing graphology, hiking, and reading mystery novels in my leisure time. The dedication to my craft extends beyond the lab—tutoring high school students has allowed me to share my knowledge with aspiring scientists, fostering a new generation's curiosity in the sciences. This dual role underscores my commitment to scientific excellence and education, values that are central to my professional journey. name: Denis Nyaga
title: Research Fellow | Newborn Genomics | Liggins Institute
bio:
I have a strong interest in human genetics, especially finding novel genes and genetic mutations that cause rare diseases. This field of biology captivates me the most. I am currently leading the establishment of NGS (Next-Generation Sequencing) for clinical diagnostics at IGENZ. 

I have previously led various clinical bioinformatics projects to identify the genetic causes rare diseases, especially in neonates and children. In addition, I have employed methods and technologies from molecular biology, bioinformatics, and computational biology to characterise the genetic susceptibility to type 1 diabetes in young children.

My academic background in biomedical and translational sciences has equipped me with the requisite knowledge and skills to be a creative and innovative individual who can adequately organise his work and drive forward research projects independently.

Managing Partner & Hi-Tech Investor @ Silicon Roundabout Ventures - Deep Tech VC If you'd like to pitch me a pre-seed/seed UK startup or if you'd like to invest in our fund as an LP, please check out the links below. I run a blog on tech, startups and VC on the Silicon Roundabout community site (link below). Currently growing the Silicon Roundabout Academy: Silicon Roundabout's e-learning platform focused on building specialist skills and work opportunities for the tech sector. Prior to Silicon Roundabout, I have worked as a C++ software engineer, web developer, and founded the boutique property investment company AGAPE Properties: 1st UK property manager to accept crypto as a payment (of which I'm still the main shareholder). As a public speaker I held guest lectures, panels and keynotes at London Fintech Week, London Tech Week, The London Institute of Banking & Finance, ASP (Politecnico di Milano), Birmingham Tech Week and the European GNSS Agency amongst others. I'm a physics, history and business geek and speak English, Italian and Spanish and love anything entrepreneurial or techie.

Entrepreneur: Prior to that, I was the CEO and co-founder at Dataflos fka Blockfenders that found its exit by joining Lirik Inc. We were a venture backed, cross border AI and data startup with offices in Palo Alto, United States and Pune, India.

VC:
I was a Venture Partner at U First Capital and a Fellow and Selection Committee Member at Berkeley Angel Network.

Education:
I have done my MBA from UC Berkeley, MS in Computer Science from UCLA, and B.Eng from Pune University.

title: Partner at Mobilize Climate Capital initiative from 3-D Energy | Investor in clean energy transition
bio: Sudheesh Sureshkumar is a Partner at Mobilize AI x Energy, a New York based investment firm investing in the picks and shovels of AI Data center power infrastructure, but based in Europe. Sudheesh has spent more than 12+ years working across European energy companies and infrastructure funds. He’s an operator-turned-entrepreneur who now invests in the Data Center x Energy Nexus. Over his career, Sudheesh has co-founded, built and commercialized both software platforms (AI-driven analytics and project finance automation for infrastructure investment funds) and energy infrastructure hardware (e.g. wind turbines). Sudheesh has end-to-end technology experience in building energy infrastructure, from deploying hardware to the power grid to navigating the intersection of data, regulation, and capital. Sudheesh is a frequent speaker in Data center conferences and other Energy and AI industry events. Sudheesh has a background in Aero-servo-elasticity and high-fidelity computing He co-holds an EU patent on Wind energy, inventing an innovative passive pitch regulation for HAWT. Sudheesh holds a Masters degree in computational engineering and structural mechanics from Blekinge Institute of Technology, Sweden.

bio:
Building IA since 2017-
IA is a multi-stage fund-led startup accelerator that invests primarily in early stage startups.

Capital. Capability. Connections. Community. That is how IA helps startups grow.

IA has 3 Pie's:
. Finvolve - INR 500 Cr corpus in SEBI Cat I & Cat II AIFs to fund Startups 
. India Accelerator - 120+ mentors providing GTM, Market Access, Technology to advise Startups 
. IA Spaces - 7K Seats, 30+ hubs across 16 cities for Startup co-working seats and events

IA's portco include:
Inc42, Matter, Ethereal Machines, Stage OTT, InCred Finance, CASHe, Imarticus Learning, Droom, NitroCommerce.ai, Zulu, Hippo Innovations, AMPL, Samosa Party, Lawyered, Optimizers, Proost, Paramount, Store Hippo, Paramount Insurance, Constems.ai, SaleAssist, Aquila Clouds, Atlas, MagicRoll.ai and more.

Invests via 
1. Accelerator Fund (INR 50 Lacs to 1 cr) - Pre Seed stage 
2. Seed Fund (INR 2-4 cr) - Seed Stage and 
3. Series A (INR 8 cr+)

Lead Frontier & Strategic Technology Deep Tech Thesis investing in AI, Vertical AI, Quantum, Semicon, Cybersecurity, Advanced Materials and Manufacturing, Physical AI and SaaS StartUps.

name: Jacob Colker
title: (Partnering with Entrepreneurs & Early Teams!) Managing Director @ AI2 Incubator
bio:
Hello, there!

I’m an early-stage investor and cofounder focused on transforming cutting-edge A.I. research into real-world companies. My expertise lies in the zero-to-one phase… the critical first two years where ideas become teams, products, and businesses.

Over the course of my career, I’ve personally raised (or helped my teams raise) more than $500 million in capital and helped create more than $2 billion in startup valuation. More importantly, I’ve had the privilege of working with exceptional founders to help them become the best versions of themselves and build their dreams.

Outside of work/family:
 
— Teach entrepreneurship at the University of Washington (foster.uw.edu)
— Play drums in a dad-rock cover band (youtube.com/@GoodLettuce)
— Black and white street/travel photography (jacobcolker.com)

title: General Partner | Emerging $200M DeepTech Fund (’26)| Exited Founder | MD @ Javelyn Technology Ventures | Angel Investor & Board Advisor | Driving Innovation, IP Commercialisation & Impact-Driven Growth
bio: As the Managing Director & Founder of Javelyn Technology Ventures, General Partner of an Emerging DeepTech Fund (‘25 ), and with over 15 years of experience in operating and investing in tech ventures, I have exercised a deep contrarian thesis conjoined with a strong conviction to help unlock potential. As an exited and experienced Founder myself I have a strong background in strategy, technology development/management, and early-stage startups as well as scale-ups. With the accumulation of an interdisciplinary education and diverse knowledge base from prestigious institutions I appreciate challenging problems and elegant solutions. My passion is to accelerate impact in the tech sector, by partnering with emerging startups that share our vision of making a lasting impact on the world. I provide them with strategic advice, capital, and network access, leveraging my expertise in start-ups, and lean methodology. Through Javelyn Technology Ventures, our financial deployment vehicle, I have invested in and advised multiple impact tech ventures across different stages and regions, in areas such as community, AI, mobility, sustainability, and health. My goal is bring visibility to markets, ventures and founders that remain underrepresented and undercapitalised.

name: Simone Severini
title: Amazon Web Services (AWS) and University College London (UCL)
location: San Francisco Bay Area United States
bio:
I'm interested in how science becomes technology. 

My background is in physics and computing, and since the late ’90s, I’ve explored various aspects of Quantum Information Processing. I earned a PhD in the then newly formed Quantum Information and Computation Group at the University of Bristol, UK, under the supervision of Richard Jozsa. I also hold a degree in Philosophy (Logic) from the University of Florence, Italy. My postdoctoral research took me to the Institute for Quantum Computing (IQC) in Waterloo, Canada. Over the years, I have held research and faculty positions at institutions including UC Berkeley, the University of Cambridge, Shanghai Jiao Tong University, and Sorbonne Université.

Before joining Amazon Web Services (AWS), I was a Professor of Physics of Information at University College London (UCL), where I helped establish Quantum Computing within the Computer Science Department and fostered industrial collaborations with companies such as Google, Lockheed Martin, and Siemens. 

At AWS, I contributed to launching Amazon Braket, the AWS Center for Quantum Computing (in partnership with Caltech), the AWS Center for Quantum Networking (in collaboration with Harvard), and the Amazon Quantum Solutions Lab. I co-founded Q&I and Phasecraft and played a role in advising some of the first quantum technology startups, including Cambridge Quantum Computing (now Quantinuum), where I was a Technical Co-Founder. I have also advised a number of private equity funds worldwide on quantum-related investments.

title: CTO at LabGenius | Angel Investor | Honorary Research Fellow in Computer Science at UCL
bio: Leo is the Co-Founder and CTO at Forgent AI, where he builds AI agents that help companies win and deliver public sector contracts. Previously, Leo served as Chief Technology Officer at LabGenius, where he was responsible for data science and machine learning (including bioinformatics), software engineering, and robotic lab automation. He has led the development of a generative AI platform as VP of Machine Learning at Odyssey Therapeutics, and was the CEO and Founder of Rahko (acquired 2021), a London-based Machine Learning SaaS company. Leo has accumulatively raised and contributed to raise nearly $550M and built teams in the Europe and the US.

title: Cures Within Reach Past SAB Chair; Felidae Conservation Fund Dir; FDL Faculty; NASA NfoLD & GeneLab AWG Mem; NSF ACCESS Champ; Peace Innovation Institute Mem; IEEE Councils Mem; MIT & Penn Mentor; OSTP, UN & NEON Advisor
company: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
bio: Dr. Clark has spent much of his research career using his training in disciplines of engineering, psychology, biochemistry/biophysics, physiology, neuroscience, and microbiology to study the evolution and biological basis of learning, memory, and intelligence. His award-winning research and patented inventions improving learning, memory, and recovery from traumatic brain injury through peripheral neuromodulation gained recognition from MacArthur fellow Dr. James McGaugh and other members of the National Academy of Sciences, USA. Dr. Clark and his colleagues' pioneering development and use of neurocybernetic prosthetics-driven targeted neuroplasticity training and cognitive-emotional restructuring inspired his work into Earth and Space personalized medicine and digital health as well as related interests involving neuroedutechnologies. Later comparative primate studies conducted with systems neuroscientist Dr. Nikos Logothetis focused on Dr. Clark’s interests in the neural basis of learning, memory, perception, and cognition across animal phylogeny, experiences that informed his newer research on statistical mechanics properties of cognitive processing, such as, but not limited to, natural and technology-based classical and quantum Hebbian learning, nonrelativistic and relativistic information processing in spatial cognition, and entropic uncertainty in language privatization, disambiguation, and structure. Dr. Clark's broader interests in the evolution of intelligence began in graduate school while working with molecular and cellular evolutionist Dr. Sidney Fox, student and colleague of Nobelists Thomas Hunt Morgan and Linus Pauling, on protocell plasticity and communication and continue today with his research on physical aspects of microbial social decision making. By creating paradigms comparing microbial goal-directed behavior with animal decision making, Dr. Clark has shown microbes learn to simulate soft-matter quantum computers, abilities mediated by classical/quantum Hebbian network attributes and putative Ca2+-dependent molecular logics and cell-response regulation. The major implications of Dr. Clark’s innovative findings regarding microbial behavior have been acknowledged by noted experts worldwide. His work extends to many topics, including host-parasite and pathogen-pathogen interactions, drug and medical device design and repurposing, neural and aneural plasticity, evolutionary and developmental transitions, extreme-environment adaptation, astrobiology, and smart computational platforms for next-generation micro- and nanobiotechnologies.

name: Ray Yang
title: Postdoctoral Research Associate in Chemistry & Computer Science
bio: I received my PhD in Physics from New Zealand Institute for Advanced Study in 2022. During my PhD, I worked with Prof. Joachim Brand developing quantum Monte Carlo algorithms for ultracold Bose gases. Later, I joined the Chemistry Department at Washington University in St. Louis as a postdoc, working with Prof. Robert Wexler on nested sampling. My extensive interdisciplinary research experience spans chemistry and physics, with published works on molecular magnetism, metallic clusters and surfaces, as well as ultracold quantum gases. My research interests focus on developing efficient and accurate computational methods for solving complicated quantum and statistical mechanical problems. title: Head of Platform Engineering and Ambassador | Expert in GitOps and Kubernetes Scalability | Published Author | Content Creator
bio: Passionate and driven Platform Engineer with a proven track record in designing, developing, and implementing efficient and scalable cloud infrastructures. Since 2021, I have been harnessing my expertise at the Hamburg Port Authority, where I've spearheaded the creation of a Kubernetes platform both on-premise and in the cloud. Implemented GitOps at scale with Argo CD, and fostered a self-sufficient environment by developing an internal developer platform. My experience at adesso as a service GmbH solidified my skills in implementing cross-cloud solutions utilizing Azure and AWS, managing Azure Public Cloud with Terraform, and addressing critical customer services. I was trusted with ensuring smooth operations and uninterrupted service for clients, which required promptly addressing any system failures. My journey began as an IT Consultant at Viada, where I administered application servers and implemented OpenShift 4 and Kubernetes, with a keen focus on security. I ensured compliance by meticulously tracking all changes and conducted regular in-house training, thereby boosting our team's competence. In every role, I have thrived on being solution-oriented and resourceful, equipped with robust skills in automation, scalability, orchestration, configuration as code (CaS), containerization, software development, and more. With a hands-on approach, I've been instrumental in forming robust DevOps teams, managing key projects, and navigating strategic planning. But to me, it never feels like work. I find joy in staying current with the latest technology trends and certifications, building proof of concepts, blogging, and networking with different manufacturers to build the best solutions with the tools available on the market. My approach has proven successful, leading to sustainable infrastructure, efficient team coordination, and the readiness to tackle upcoming challenges with agility and resilience. Driven by my personal passion, I am eager to continue leveraging my expertise to build innovative solutions and contribute to the field of Cloud Computing.

name: Luke Ashe-browne
title: SRE, Devops, Kubernetes, CI/CD Consultant/Engineer
bio:
With over 25 years of experience, I bridge the gap between complex engineering and commercial strategy. As a Director and Consulting Architect, I specialise in building high-performance architectures and leading multi-disciplinary teams across Insurance and Finance/ Fin-tech, Media, Prop-tech, and E-commerce.

My recent focus has been on the convergence of Cloud Native Platform Engineering and Modern Data Stack Architecture. I act as a strategic stakeholder for business case design, product road-maps, and delivery oversight—ensuring technology is a primary driver of commercial ROI.

Strategic Data & Platform Leadership:
I lead large-scale programs to deliver Data Platforms that move beyond simple storage into "Data-as-a-Product" ecosystems. My recent projects focus on:

ARCHITECTURE: Designing tiered/Medallion data warehouse structures (Bronze/Silver/Gold) and implementing Data Contracts to ensure reliability.
DATA STACK: Orchestrating modern tool-sets including Snowflake, dbt, Airflow (Astronomer), and AWS Glue.
GOVERNANCE & QUALITY: Implementing Data Governance frameworks using Collate, and ensuring platform observability and trust through Monte Carlo.
MACHINE LEARNING OPS: Integrating technologies such as Kubeflow to bridge the gap between data engineering and AI/ML productionalization.

Cloud & DevOps Foundations:
As an ongoing practitioner, I maintain deep expertise in AWS, GCP, and Kubernetes. I specialize in building Internal Developer Platforms (IDP) that emphasize self-service, GitOps adoption, and developer experience (DevEx).
Core Technology & Expertise:
LANGAUGES: Rust, GoLang, Python, NodeJS/Typescript, PHP.
Data: Snowflake, dbt, Airflow/Astronomer, AWS Glue, Collate, Monte Carlo, various SQL/NoSQL platforms.
Infrastructure: Terraform, Kubernetes (EKS/GKE/On-prem), Kubeflow.
Leadership: Consulting Engagement, Technical Pre-sales, Department Structuring, and Budgetary Oversight.


Specialties: Dev Ops, docker containerisation, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, Configuration management (Ansible, Puppet, Salt), Virtualisation, Monitoring, Metrics, Logging, PHP, Python, GoLang, Scala, Javascript, NodeJS, MySQL, Posgresql, UniData, Java, Linux administration, Open Source solutions.

title: AWS Community Builder | DevOps Engineer | Kubernetes | AWS Certified at GFT Group
bio:
I work with SaaS companies that are scaling fast and feeling the pressure of rising cloud costs, unreliable deployments, and infrastructure that wasn’t built for growth.

As a Fractional CTO and Platform Engineer with 16+ years of experience, I help teams regain control of their cloud architecture, reduce AWS spend, and build scalable systems that support rapid product expansion — without slowing down engineering velocity.

Through Schottz Advisory, I partner with founders and leadership teams to solve high-impact challenges such as:

• Cloud costs growing faster than revenue
• Infrastructure bottlenecks limiting product scalability
• Deployment processes creating risk and instability
• Lack of senior technical leadership during critical growth phases

Recent outcomes I’ve delivered include:

• Reduced cloud costs by 30%+ through architecture redesign and FinOps practices
• Improved deployment reliability and incident response for high-traffic platforms
• Designed AWS & Kubernetes infrastructures capable of supporting rapid user growth
• Implemented DevOps workflows that increased deployment speed while reducing risk

I operate as a strategic technical partner — not just an executor — helping companies make smarter architecture decisions that balance scalability, reliability, and cost.

Engagement models include:

• Fractional CTO leadership
• Cloud architecture and infrastructure optimization
• DevOps and platform engineering strategy
• High-performance execution through my consulting network

If your team is scaling and your infrastructure is becoming harder to manage, I help bring clarity, stability, and cost efficiency — without the overhead of a full-time executive.

bio: I’m an NLP researcher with a PhD in Artificial Intelligence from Sapienza University of Rome, specializing in factuality evaluation and language model reliability. My work focuses on building resources and metrics (like LLM-OASIS and FENICE) to assess the factuality of LLM outputs. Passionate about bridging academic research and applied AI, I’m particularly interested in evaluation methodologies, retrieval-augmented generation, and modular pipelines for trustworthy NLP.

bio:
I am a senior applied scientist at Thomson Reuters Labs. I work on improving AI assistant tools for legal professionals using LLMs.

I hold a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering from Pohang University of Science and Technology. I have extensive knowledge and experience with deep learning in the natural language processing and machine translation fields in both academia and industry.

I am interested in all areas related to multilingual and multimodal natural language analysis using machine learning with applications to natural language processing, information retrieval, and machine translation.

name: 宝锋 王
title: AD Parking System Overall Engineering PIC
bio: --自然生长出的汽车人 出于少年时期对汽车的热爱，从本科到博士一直研修汽车工程专业，属于自然生长出的汽车人。本硕博期间通过对力学、机械、液压液力、材料、电工电子及控制等相关基础学科，以及汽车构造、车辆系统动力学与控制、汽车电子等专业课的学习，打下了坚实的专业基础；通过耳濡目染打下了深刻的行业烙印，因此从机械、电子、控制、行业及法律法规对汽车都有较为深刻的认识。 --自然延伸的码农 硕博期间就读于北京理工大学主动安全实验室，在自动驾驶远未走红的2000年前后，实验室便已经开始了对CCS，ACC相关辅助驾驶系统的研究--原因很简单，ACC是实验室一贯研究方向--ABS和ASR--的自然延续。作为实验室新成员，一方面继续车辆动力学相关的研究，一方面接过ACC环境感知的新担子，从毫米波雷达到机器视觉，从多目标跟踪到机器学习和传感器融合。很庆幸自己的学术背景可以如此自然地从传统汽车行业过度到一个全新的领域智能驾驶，而自己也如此自然的从汽车人延伸到算法工程师和码农。由于自己经历了实验室的ADAS车载感知系统是从无到有的过程，因此除了算法本身以外，对传感器的选型、安装及标定也有更全面的了解。此外，由于自身的专业背景，因此在系统功能开发过程中对车规、ISO/SAE标准、AutoSAR框架也有一定的关注。 --驾龄与驾驶经验 出于专业原因，大一时就考取了驾照，之后便一直开车（从纯机械人车交互，到control-by-wire），时至今日驾龄已超10年（0事故），并在欧洲和美国都有很长历程的驾驶经验。作为汽车人，驾驶过程中对车辆的动力、操稳、制动稳定性、平顺性都有了更深刻的理解。而且开车的同时也锻炼了故障诊断和维修的能力，从window regulator到swaybar-link，从engine trunk noise到制动系统排气，自己都有排查修复过；并且在美国求学阶段也通过为二手车购买者提供mechanical check和test drive服务来补贴家用。同时，通过test drive不同的车也对不同品牌汽车有了更直接的体会。

I know the basics of lidar, familar with the perception system for automous driving system especially for lidar based 3D object detection, segmentation tasks. I am familar with Python, C++, ROS, Apollo, and deep learning framework Pytorch. I have a good habit of reading and keeping track of the frontier papers, and can learn and reproduce the good ideas. Earlier I was a product development engineer at SAIC-Volkswagen R&D department, know well of the design and test of the automobile product. I am used to working in a multi culture and multi department environment. I have background of robotics and automobil industry, I am familar with both hardware and software and know fundamentals of perception, localization, planning and control system.

title: CRO, GM, SVP / GTM Leader / Media Exec / SAAS Sales / Multiple Exits (Oracle, Uber, Marketo, Adobe, IAS)
bio: Enterprise AI leader with a track record of building markets for voice AI, inference and model observability in collaboration with Mistral AI, Together AI, Hugging Face, and others. Expert at deploying specialized sales and Forward Deployed Engineering teams inspired by OpenAI and Palantir to drive rapid enterprise adoption. Architected custom consulting, implementation, and agent engineering functions for major clients, delivering measurable business outcomes and defining new standards for enterprise AI software integration. Results driven, strategic thinker and operator with deep industry rolodex and proven success building companies and running P&Ls – from venture backed start-ups to multi-billion dollar enterprises. Customer-obsessed sales leader with extensive experience in leading, mentoring, coaching, scaling and motivating teams of top sales performers. Stellar track record of driving and exceeding revenue growth in North America as well as EMEA and APAC. Extensive experience managing Board and investor relationships. Vik has a stellar career with a focus on Enterprise sales, Partnerships and strategy with AI start ups like Google Gemini / Open AI / Perplexity, Windsurf. Additionally he has held Global C level agency leadership positions with Meta, Google Gemini, WPP - working across digital agencies, media services agencies, data / technology - driving value for many Fortune 500 companies including Unilever, AT&T, VW, PepsiCo, Airbnb, Samsung, Procter & Gamble, Bank of America, Kellogg’s, Visa, Amazon to name a few. Known for bridging AGI, SAAS Software, Advertising, Technology, Digital Media and Capital, as well as having a global digital perspective, Vik is one of the most sought-after thought leaders in the business; he has appeared at countless conferences and panels and is regularly quoted in media including Wall Street Journal, New York Times, Advertising Age, CNBC, CNN, Bloomberg and more.

name: Sarah Friar
title: CFO OpenAI | Co-Launcher @ Ladies Who Launch | Board Member @ Walmart, ConsenSys, Operation HOPE | Trustee Stanford University | Advisory Board Blavatnik School | Aspen Fellow | OBE | N.Irish
bio: Most recently, Sarah Friar was chief executive officer of Nextdoor, the neighborhood network that connects neighborhood stakeholders, including neighbors, businesses, and public services, online and in real life to build stronger, more vibrant, and resilient neighborhoods. She helped take the company public in 2021 under the ticker NYSE:KIND. Prior to Nextdoor, Sarah served as chief financial officer at Square (now known as Block, Inc.). Under Sarah’s leadership, the company launched its initial public offering in 2015 and added $30 billion in market capitalization. Before her tenure at Square, Sarah served as senior vice president of finance & strategy at Salesforce. Sarah also held executive roles at Goldman Sachs, as well as leadership positions at McKinsey in both London and South Africa. Sarah currently also serves on the boards of Walmart and of Consensys, a private company in the Web3 arena, and she previously served on the boards of Slack Technologies (from 2017 to 2021), Dragonneer Growth Opportunities Corp. (from 2020 to 2021), Dragonneer Growth Opportunities Corp. II (from 2020 to 2021), Dragonneer Growth Opportunities Corp. III (from 2021 to 2023), and New Relic (from 2013 to 2018). She is a Fellow of the inaugural class of the Finance Leaders Fellowship Program, a member of the Aspen Global Leadership Network, and serves on the Board of Trustees of Stanford University and on the advisory board of Operation HOPE. She is co-founder of Ladies Who Launch, a network that mentors and inspires women entrepreneurs and business owners. She was named to the Time100 2026 most influential people and the 2023 NACD Directorship 100 selection, an annual recognition of the leading corporate directors, corporate governance experts, policymakers, and influencers who significantly impact boardroom practices and performance.  Sarah grew up in Northern Ireland and earned her MEng in Metallurgy, Economics, and Management from the University of Oxford and her MBA from the Stanford University Graduate School of Business, where she graduated as an Arjay Miller scholar. In 2019 she was granted an OBE from Queen Elizabeth II for services to entrepreneurship. In her spare time she loves to hike, read and travel.

bio:
I strive to bring structure and heart to every square foot. With deep experience leading workplace and real estate strategy at some of the world’s most innovative companies, I help teams scale globally while staying grounded in what matters: people, purpose, and potential. From orchestrating office expansions and designing spaces that inspire, to shaping thoughtful policies around food, transportation, and events—I thrive at the intersection of operational excellence and employee experience.

As President of CoreNet NorCal, I’m also passionate about growing our community, elevating future leaders, and sparking meaningful conversations about the future of work.

Let’s build what’s next—smarter, bolder, and better together.

View my office projects at http://www.flickr.com/photos/tracylouisehawkins/

Specialties: Leadership of global teams - C-suite collaboration - Project Management - specifically running multiple, cross geographical projects in parallel. Facilities/Workplace Management, Standardization and Design. CRE Planning & Transactions, Change and Budget Management. Procurement and vendor negotiations. Corporate travel programs. Events and connections.

bio: I’m an AI product leader and serial entrepreneur passionate about building the next generation of Agentic AI systems — where intelligent agents can reason, plan, and act autonomously on behalf of users and businesses. Currently serving as Vice President at Manus AI and Head of Product & Business at Monica AI, I focus on shaping AI assistant platforms into truly agentic ecosystems — blending LLMs, contextual memory, and multi-step decision frameworks to empower both individuals and organizations. My journey spans over a decade across product innovation, business strategy, and entrepreneurship, including two successful exits. I’ve led teams from idea to scale, built platforms reaching 10M+ global users, and developed deep expertise at the intersection of AI, product design, and user engagement. I’m driven by one core belief — that the future of human-AI collaboration lies not in passive assistants, but in autonomous, trustworthy, and human-aligned agents capable of turning intent into intelligent action.

name: Akshay Jagadeesh
title: Research Scientist at OpenAI: AI Safety + Health AI
bio: I am a scientist working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and neuroscience. My career began with a focus on understanding how the brain enables perception and behavior, using computational models to connect neural activity with cognition. After nearly a decade of academic research, including a PhD at Stanford University and a postdoctoral fellowship at Harvard Medical School, I have transitioned into industry to apply these insights more broadly. I am currently a Researcher at OpenAI, where I focus on two goals: advancing safety research to ensure artificial intelligence systems are reliable and aligned, and exploring how AI can accelerate progress in health and medicine. I am especially motivated by the opportunity to translate my background in neuroscience and modeling into building AI tools that both deepen scientific discovery and contribute to human well-being. At the core of my work is a curiosity about intelligent systems—both biological and artificial—and a commitment to using that understanding to create technologies that are safe, responsible, and transformative.

title: VP Product @ Workday
location: New York City Metropolitan Area United States
bio:
Product executive focused on building enterprise platforms that scale intelligently, operate globally, and center the employee experience. Currently leading product management for Google’s People Products & Technologies group, overseeing strategy and execution for the systems that power HR with an emphasis on AI enablement, privacy-by-design architecture, and cross-functional platform innovation.

Previously spent over a decade at Workday driving product strategy across CHRO, CFO, and COO domains. Built and scaled teams responsible for payroll, core HCM, and employee experience. Known for a leadership style that blends executional rigor with platform vision and deep customer empathy.

Frequent speaker on digital transformation, AI in the workplace, and inclusive product design. Passionate about growing high-performing, mission-driven teams that turn complexity into clarity and ideas into impact.

bio: I am currently working as a Product Director at Google, and my main responsibility is to ensure that Google's product lines meet the needs of users and achieve commercial success. My purpose of using Linkedin is to meet the best people in the industry, to share my expertise and to learn about the future of different fields. 1Develop and execute the company's product strategy. Needs to understand market trends, competitive environment and user needs, work with senior management team to define product vision and goals, and develop roadmap and strategy accordingly. 2 Collaborate with the product team to define product features and functionality, develop product development plans, and ensure that products are delivered on time and meet quality standards. Also need to be responsible for product lifecycle management, including product improvement, update and termination decisions. 3 needs to work with various departments, including design, engineering, marketing, operations and customer support. They need to work closely with these teams to ensure overall consistency and synergy of the product. They also need to communicate with senior management and coordinate the needs and priorities of various stakeholders. 4 Need to analyze and monitor the competitive market situation. Need to understand competitors' product strategies and dynamics, and adjust product strategies and plans in a timely manner based on market trends and feedback. 5 Collaborate with marketing team to provide product promotion and marketing support. Need to define the core value proposition of the product and collaborate with the marketing team on marketing campaigns to ensure product awareness and market share growth. Overall, my current role is to ensure that Google's product line meets user needs, is successful in the marketplace, and works with various departments to achieve product planning, development, and promotion. Market insight, strategic planning skills and team management skills are required to drive continued product innovation and commercial success.

name: Nicolas Lang
title: Sr. Consultant - AI Technical Product manager: Driving GenAI solutions from research to enterprise value.
bio: As a Deployment Strategist at Mistral, I am ensuring enterprises unlock the full value of AI through strategy alignment, product management, and use case deployment. I believe AI’s true impact in the enterprise comes from ownership (your data, your models) and deep customization to fit real-world needs. With 7 years in GenAI, I’ve bridged the gap between cutting-edge research and high-impact solutions, from pioneering GPT for music generation in China to producing Oblivion: Remastered (4M players in its first week). My experience spans FSI, Healthcare and Creative Industries. I’ve led cross-functional teams, delivered AI platforms to 20,000+ users, and aligned AI with executive vision, leveraging fluency in Mandarin, English, and French. As a Deployment Strategist at Mistral AI, I now focus on making sovereign, tailored AI a reality for enterprises, combining my technical depth, product instinct, and passion for turning complex challenges into scalable, user-centric solutions. Feel free to connect!

bio: AI Applied Engineer @ Mistral AI I build AI systems that solve real problems. At Mistral, I’m part of a dynamic team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible with large language models and applied AI. My work is about turning cutting-edge research into practical, scalable solutions—whether it’s automating workflows, improving evaluation frameworks, or deploying models that make a difference. I thrive in fast-moving environments where innovation meets execution, guided by the belief that “whether you think you can, or you think you can’t—you’re right.” Before diving into AI full-time, I explored the intersection of sustainability and technology, organizing events like the EPFL Sustainable Innovation Challenge to connect ideas with action. That experience reinforced my passion for building tools that empower people and create impact. I’m always up for a conversation about AI, engineering, or how technology can drive meaningful change. Let’s connect!

name: Vik Kathuria
title: CRO, GM, SVP / GTM Leader / Media Exec / SAAS Sales / Multiple Exits (Oracle, Uber, Marketo, Adobe, IAS)
bio: Enterprise AI leader with a track record of building markets for voice AI, inference and model observability in collaboration with Mistral AI, Together AI, Hugging Face, and others. Expert at deploying specialized sales and Forward Deployed Engineering teams inspired by OpenAI and Palantir to drive rapid enterprise adoption. Architected custom consulting, implementation, and agent engineering functions for major clients, delivering measurable business outcomes and defining new standards for enterprise AI software integration. Results driven, strategic thinker and operator with deep industry rolodex and proven success building companies and running P&Ls – from venture backed start-ups to multi-billion dollar enterprises. Customer-obsessed sales leader with extensive experience in leading, mentoring, coaching, scaling and motivating teams of top sales performers. Stellar track record of driving and exceeding revenue growth in North America as well as EMEA and APAC. Extensive experience managing Board and investor relationships. Vik has a stellar career with a focus on Enterprise sales, Partnerships and strategy with AI start ups like Google Gemini / Open AI / Perplexity, Windsurf. Additionally he has held Global C level agency leadership positions with Meta, Google Gemini, WPP - working across digital agencies, media services agencies, data / technology - driving value for many Fortune 500 companies including Unilever, AT&T, VW, PepsiCo, Airbnb, Samsung, Procter & Gamble, Bank of America, Kellogg’s, Visa, Amazon to name a few. Known for bridging AGI, SAAS Software, Advertising, Technology, Digital Media and Capital, as well as having a global digital perspective, Vik is one of the most sought-after thought leaders in the business; he has appeared at countless conferences and panels and is regularly quoted in media including Wall Street Journal, New York Times, Advertising Age, CNBC, CNN, Bloomberg and more.

title: CFO OpenAI | Co-Launcher @ Ladies Who Launch | Board Member @ Walmart, ConsenSys, Operation HOPE | Trustee Stanford University | Advisory Board Blavatnik School | Aspen Fellow | OBE | N.Irish
bio: Most recently, Sarah Friar was chief executive officer of Nextdoor, the neighborhood network that connects neighborhood stakeholders, including neighbors, businesses, and public services, online and in real life to build stronger, more vibrant, and resilient neighborhoods. She helped take the company public in 2021 under the ticker NYSE:KIND. Prior to Nextdoor, Sarah served as chief financial officer at Square (now known as Block, Inc.). Under Sarah’s leadership, the company launched its initial public offering in 2015 and added $30 billion in market capitalization. Before her tenure at Square, Sarah served as senior vice president of finance & strategy at Salesforce. Sarah also held executive roles at Goldman Sachs, as well as leadership positions at McKinsey in both London and South Africa. Sarah currently also serves on the boards of Walmart and of Consensys, a private company in the Web3 arena, and she previously served on the boards of Slack Technologies (from 2017 to 2021), Dragonneer Growth Opportunities Corp. (from 2020 to 2021), Dragonneer Growth Opportunities Corp. II (from 2020 to 2021), Dragonneer Growth Opportunities Corp. III (from 2021 to 2023), and New Relic (from 2013 to 2018). She is a Fellow of the inaugural class of the Finance Leaders Fellowship Program, a member of the Aspen Global Leadership Network, and serves on the Board of Trustees of Stanford University and on the advisory board of Operation HOPE. She is co-founder of Ladies Who Launch, a network that mentors and inspires women entrepreneurs and business owners. She was named to the Time100 2026 most influential people and the 2023 NACD Directorship 100 selection, an annual recognition of the leading corporate directors, corporate governance experts, policymakers, and influencers who significantly impact boardroom practices and performance.  Sarah grew up in Northern Ireland and earned her MEng in Metallurgy, Economics, and Management from the University of Oxford and her MBA from the Stanford University Graduate School of Business, where she graduated as an Arjay Miller scholar. In 2019 she was granted an OBE from Queen Elizabeth II for services to entrepreneurship. In her spare time she loves to hike, read and travel.

bio:
I strive to bring structure and heart to every square foot. With deep experience leading workplace and real estate strategy at some of the world’s most innovative companies, I help teams scale globally while staying grounded in what matters: people, purpose, and potential. From orchestrating office expansions and designing spaces that inspire, to shaping thoughtful policies around food, transportation, and events—I thrive at the intersection of operational excellence and employee experience.

As President of CoreNet NorCal, I’m also passionate about growing our community, elevating future leaders, and sparking meaningful conversations about the future of work.

Let’s build what’s next—smarter, bolder, and better together.

View my office projects at http://www.flickr.com/photos/tracylouisehawkins/

Specialties: Leadership of global teams - C-suite collaboration - Project Management - specifically running multiple, cross geographical projects in parallel. Facilities/Workplace Management, Standardization and Design. CRE Planning & Transactions, Change and Budget Management. Procurement and vendor negotiations. Corporate travel programs. Events and connections.

name: Chris Conant
title: CEO Zennify
bio: Operator-builder with 25+ years leading growth, transformations, and exits across SaaS, services, and data/AI. Ex-Salesforce SVP who oversaw retention and expansion for a $16B+ customer base across North America, LATAM & Global Public Sector. Former CEO of Zennify, the data/AI-first consulting firm for regulated industries. Now at Anthropic as Global Head of Strategic Deployments & Customer Success, leading the global teams (Forward Deployed Engineering & Customer Success) that help enterprises actually put AI to work, not just experiment with it. After 25 years at the intersection of technology, people, and process, the lesson that stuck is that the technology is rarely the hard part. Changing how people work is. The goal that drives me is simple: help people do better work and get their time back for the things that matter. Core strengths: P&L leadership, AI & data strategy, Customer Success, GTM orchestration, large-scale transformations, M&A integration.

name: Sar Warner
title: Chief of Staff at Patreon | Strategy 🔮, Operations ⚙️, Culture 🌎
location: San Francisco Bay Area United States
bio:
👋 💁🏻‍♀️🌉 👶🏻

⬅️ I swore I'd never work a desk job; attending meeting after meeting, wearing starched, uncomfortable clothes, and sitting for hours at a time, all underneath a beige office umbrella felt like my version of hell. So when I found myself discontentedly bouncing from a job working on a lacrosse field, to a job in a Title I school, to a job at UC Berkeley, you can imagine my confusion. 

➡️ It turns out that I really love desk jobs; a well run meeting gives me deep satisfaction, I like putting on real pants on office days, I often get lost in thought for hours at a time doing deep focus work, and the buildings I've had the privilege of working in aren't beige at all. I never thought "desk jobs" could provide me the opportunities they have; improving collaboration and decision-making among leaders, planning and executing an $800K C-Suite event, helping an organization launch products more effectively, the list goes on. The common thread is developing individuals, teams, and organizations to be the best versions of themselves and Anthropic is the most interesting challenge yet. In many ways, I'm just getting started here, and I can't wait to see what happens. 🚀 💕

name: Courtney Barno
title: Chief Operating Officer, Defense Unicorns 🦄
location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
bio:
I love building teams, systems, and clarity. My favorite work sits at the intersection of strategy and execution, especially inside organizations that are growing fast and solving meaningful problems.

As COO of a venture-backed defense tech startup, I helped scale the company from less than $3M to more than $30M ARR and grew the team from 30 to 200. I built the operating rhythms that supported that growth, partnered closely with the founders, and worked across sales, revenue, product, delivery, people, and legal. We achieved 0 percent customer churn and raised a $35M Series A.

After that experience, I returned to government because I wanted to bring what I learned back to the mission. My time at JSOC gave me a front row seat to the real barriers that make technology adoption hard. It also showed me how much opportunity there is for founders who care about solving real operational problems with the right technology.

Today, I support deep tech and dual use teams through my LLC while I explore my next high-leverage role. I’m energized by companies building ambitious products, caring about their mission, and looking for an operator who brings clarity, follow-through, and a bias toward action.

I thrive in ambiguity, I like details, and I’m at my best when I’m building something that matters.

bio:
I have spent my career at the intersection of technology, policy, and communications helping organizations navigate the moments that define how they're understood and trusted.

At Anthropic, I lead the Strategic Advisory function within Central Policy. My team develops Anthropic's policy positions, builds the research and collateral that drives real-world outcomes, and makes sure our policy teams have what they need to be effective advocates.

Before Anthropic, I was a Managing Director at Breakwater Strategy, where I led high-stakes strategic communications and public affairs work for frontier AI labs, applied-AI startups, energy innovators, media organizations, and privacy tech companies facing defining moments in growth, regulation, or reinvention. name: Kacie Jenkins
title: SVP Marketing at Sendoso | Former Sourcegraph, early Fastly (took them public), and Roku
bio: I’ve been building beloved brands and scaling high-growth startups since 2008. Things I get excited about: Partnering with customer-obsessed founders and leaders who prioritize doing the right thing over growth at all costs. Building exceptional AI-enabled teams that use thoughtful automation to unlock time for thinking ahead, coming up with big, original ideas and building strong relationships with customers and prospects. Redefining marketing and growth as AI diminishes the impact of traditional channel plays and credibility, trust, and human connection become a competitive advantage. Creating trust loops that fuel efficient hyper-growth through meaningful, memorable brand experiences, community engagement and authentic executive thought leadership. Customer-first, full lifecycle marketing that powers retention and expansion. Marketing isn’t succeeding unless our customers are growing with us long term. About me: I’m currently the Head of Marketing for Claude Code at Anthropic. I was previously the SVP of Marketing at Sendoso, where I: Rebuilt a lean, high impact marketing team from the ground up. Owned 100% of qualified pipeline generation, creating over 9 figures of pipeline while partnering with Sales to improve win rates, increase ACV and scale revenue - with a flat budget and headcount. Established Sendoso as the category leader, helping to acquire our top two competitors and turn the business around to dominate the market. Before Sendoso, I helped take Fastly from a 25-person startup to $200M ARR and scale through a hugely successful IPO. I’ve led marketing at Sourcegraph, a dev tools company, where I helped grow revenue 4x year-over-year, and at Ace Hotel Group, a beloved global hospitality brand. I helped build Roku into the leading streaming company in North America. I support companies with: - target market and ICP definition - building high performing marketing teams - dialing in go-to-market strategy - bold positioning and storytelling - creating and defending new categories - tightening up pipeline forecasting and generation - standing up an ABM operating model - building founder brands that drive pipeline - standing up employee advocacy programs - unlocking community-driven growth - navigating the many exciting challenges of scaleups.

name: Hannah Pritchett
title: Binti now, Stripe + Facebook then. Operations nerd, book nerd, analogy nerd.
bio: I’m an operator, specifically one of those old-time telephone operators, running a giant switchboard to connect people and get things done. I’m a bridge between engineering and operations, between people and problems, between domains that look different but are the same if you squint. My resume may look random, but that's because I'm most energized when I go to rapidly growing teams where the company most needs an operator, even if I don't yet speak the language. In my former life as a linguist I moved abroad with only rudimentary language training and quickly learned enough to rent myself an apartment in Egyptian Arabic, find a side gig as a radio show host in Indonesian, and talk my way out of being arrested in a combo of Vietnamese and French (long story). No matter the domain, I find patterns, tell stories with data, stay calm in chaos, bring out the best in my teams, and get results. I love public speaking, people development, coaching and advice-giving, thinking in extended analogies, collecting trivia factoids (as a proud Jeopardy! loser), and reading anything and everything.

name: Caity White
title: Senior Product Manager at Google | Product Development | Product Lifecycle Management |  Product Marketing | Business Development | AI Strategist |  NYU Stern MBA
bio: With over two decades of entrepreneurial expertise at Google and other organizations, I consistently play a key role in pioneering the development of world-class products, including the visions, strategies, and teams needed to design, market and deploy them. I am passionate about creating the best quality product while managing complex matrixed organizations, stakeholders, and requirements in a dynamic and ever-changing tech-landscape. My journey at Google began as an Engineering Program Manager, where I led multiple projects complementing the Google Pixel smartphone, before advancing to the role of Product Manager for the Pixel Watch. In this capacity, I spearheaded the vision, conceptualization, and execution of next-generation hardware and software products, collaborating with cross-functional teams to drive sustainable multi year business strategies. In my current role as Senior Product Manager for the ongoing Pixel Watch line, I leverage user-driven data and insights to inform product decisions and optimize performance. My ability to collaborate with diverse stakeholders, parse user needs and market data, while managing technical requirements is fundamental to driving product success—both in defining product requirements and creating new and unique experiences for users around the globe. Even beyond product development, I love working with people and supporting employee enrichment. As a member of the Women in Hardware employee resource group, I championed the enhancement of female and gender-diverse user adoption across Pixel products. I also served in the Google Mentor Program where I coached junior product managers to enable their career advancement and foster a culture of inclusivity and growth. name: Jane Leibrock
title: Head of User Experience Research at Anthropic
bio: Hi, I’m Jane Leibrock, the head of brand at Even, a company helping people make smart decisions about money. I’m a trained user researcher, and previously worked for Facebook and Barack Obama’s 2008 presidential campaign. As a field organizer on the Obama campaign, I became fascinated with the power of the Obama brand. Getting plunked down in new areas — Anchorage, AK, and then Henderson, NV — showed me how people related to the campaign in different ways. I wondered how it all formed one cohesive message, and how the people I met formed their opinions. So I decided to become a user researcher. After getting my master’s from the University of Michigan’s School of Information, I took a research job at Facebook in 2011. While there, I researched how people interacted with groups, their profile pages, and the News Feed. I also did brand research for Instagram, looked into how teens related to Facebook, and to what degree people trusted Facebook. Eventually, I managed the Friend Sharing research team. I most enjoyed projects that brought me close to Facebook’s communication design and content strategy teams. A hackathon project that I product managed launched and remains live today (it’s called Save for Later). In early 2015, Even called. I joined the company as its first employee, drawn to the company’s mission of freeing people from the stress of living paycheck to paycheck. name: Savina Hawkins
title: Senior UX Researcher | Working on Something New!
bio:
My work sits at the intersection of artificial intelligence, product, market and customer research, informed by my academic background in AI from Stanford and Harvard, where I graduated with distinction. I've consistently bridged the gap between complex technology and human needs, from building Eventbrite's UXR function to developing AI products at Google.

Having experienced firsthand the challenges of deriving actionable insights from massive amounts of customer data, I'm now focused on democratizing access to high-quality customer intelligence through AI. I frequently speak and write about the future of AI-powered research, ethical AI development, and the evolution of customer understanding in the digital age.

Currently building the future of customer intelligence, backed by our work with leading tech companies and our growing community of product and research leaders.

name: Nicolas Solomita
title: Artificial Intelligence & Data @Deloitte Luxembourg | Generative AI | Machine Learning | Natural Language Processing
bio: Nicolas is an Deployment Strategist @Mistral AI, helping organisations adopt open and sovereign Generative AI. As part of Mistral AI's strategic partnership with the Government of Luxembourg, he helps public-sector institutions take Mistral AI from strategy and use-case discovery through to secure, sovereign, production-grade deployment, leading workstreams across model deployment, public-sector AI assistants, and domain-specific use cases. His focus is making sure GenAI doesn't just look good on a slide, but is deployed securely, adopted widely, and trusted in real environments. Before Mistral AI, Nicolas was a Senior Data Scientist @Deloitte Luxembourg's AI & Data team, working with public and private sector clients as well as European institutions. He led and contributed to multiple Generative AI and NLP projects, taking them from early ideation all the way to industrialisation. His experience spans text classification, information extraction, text generation (LLMs), automatic speech recognition, and the development of complete data and model pipelines. Nicolas holds degrees in Computer Science (BSc) and Data Science (MSc), and began his career as a Data Engineer building big data platforms and cloud-based data management solutions. This end-to-end background, from infrastructure to strategy, is what lets him bridge the gap between ambitious AI ideas and solutions that work reliably in production.

name: Nicolas Lang
title: Sr. Consultant - AI Technical Product manager: Driving GenAI solutions from research to enterprise value.
bio: As a Deployment Strategist at Mistral, I am ensuring enterprises unlock the full value of AI through strategy alignment, product management, and use case deployment. I believe AI’s true impact in the enterprise comes from ownership (your data, your models) and deep customization to fit real-world needs. With 7 years in GenAI, I’ve bridged the gap between cutting-edge research and high-impact solutions, from pioneering GPT for music generation in China to producing Oblivion: Remastered (4M players in its first week). My experience spans FSI, Healthcare and Creative Industries. I’ve led cross-functional teams, delivered AI platforms to 20,000+ users, and aligned AI with executive vision, leveraging fluency in Mandarin, English, and French. As a Deployment Strategist at Mistral AI, I now focus on making sovereign, tailored AI a reality for enterprises, combining my technical depth, product instinct, and passion for turning complex challenges into scalable, user-centric solutions. Feel free to connect!

bio:
I like helping exceptional technologists build companies and products that realize their vision.
